reference.source: OMIM / GeneReviews (NCBI) and standard clinical genetics texts
clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive disorder of lysosome-related organelle biogenesis with several genetic subtypes (for example HPS1 through HPS to AP3B1)
Core triad is oculocutaneous albinism, a bleeding tendency from absent platelet dense granules, and accumulation of ceroid lipofuscin in tissues
Ocular features include reduced visual acuity, nystagmus, photophobia and iris transillumination
The platelet storage-pool defect causes easy bruising, epistaxis and prolonged bleeding despite a normal platelet count
HPS1 and HPS4 subtypes are prone to progressive pulmonary fibrosis, typically in adulthood, a major cause of mortality
Granulomatous colitis resembling inflammatory bowel disease occurs in some subtypes
The AP3B1 (HPS2) and BLOC subtype HPS10 are associated with immunodeficiency and recurrent infection
Diagnosis rests on demonstrating absent platelet dense granules on whole-mount electron microscopy alongside molecular testing
reference.pathophysiology: Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome results from biallelic variants in genes encoding subunits of protein complexes (including AP-3 and the biogenesis of lysosome-related organelle complexes, BLOC) that direct cargo to lysosome-related organelles. Defective biogenesis impairs melanosomes (albinism), platelet dense granules (bleeding) and other specialised organelles. Progressive accumulation of ceroid lipofuscin and dysregulated lysosomal function in the lung and gut contribute to pulmonary fibrosis and granulomatous colitis in susceptible subtypes.
additionalDifferentials: Inherited platelet function disorders and storage-pool disease
Inflammatory bowel disease when colitis predominates
additionalInvestigations: Whole-mount electron microscopy of platelets showing absent dense granules
Molecular genetic testing across the known HPS genes
High-resolution CT of the chest and pulmonary function tests for fibrosis surveillance
Ophthalmological assessment including visual acuity and iris transillumination
Colonoscopy and biopsy when granulomatous colitis is suspected
redFlags: Progressive breathlessness or restrictive pattern suggesting pulmonary fibrosis
Significant or unexplained bleeding, particularly around surgery or childbirth
Recurrent severe infection in immunodeficiency-associated subtypes
Refractory colitis with weight loss and systemic upset
reference.prognosis: Prognosis depends on subtype: pigmentary and bleeding features are lifelong but manageable, whereas subtypes prone to pulmonary fibrosis (notably HPS1 and HPS4) have a substantially reduced life expectancy from progressive respiratory failure.
pitfalls: Attributing the bleeding tendency to a low platelet count rather than a functional dense-granule defect
Failing to arrange respiratory surveillance in fibrosis-prone subtypes
Overlooking bleeding risk before surgical or dental procedures
Mislabelling the granulomatous colitis as classic inflammatory bowel disease
management: Manage the platelet storage-pool bleeding tendency with antifibrinolytics such as tranexamic acid, desmopressin, and platelet transfusion to cover surgery or significant haemorrhage, while avoiding aspirin and other antiplatelet agents
Address oculocutaneous albinism with strict photoprotection, refractive correction, low-vision aids and regular skin examination for malignancy

Undertake pulmonary fibrosis surveillance with high-resolution CT and lung function in fibrosis-prone subtypes such as HPS1 and HPS4, considering antifibrotic therapy and referral for lung transplantation
Treat granulomatous colitis along inflammatory bowel disease lines with aminosalicylates, corticosteroids, immunosuppression or biologic therapy
Advise pre-procedure haematology planning and alert anaesthetic and surgical teams to the bleeding risk before any intervention
Coordinate multidisciplinary care across haematology, respiratory medicine, ophthalmology, dermatology and gastroenterology
Offer genetic counselling and family testing given autosomal recessive inheritance across the HPS gene subtypes
